work_completed: Addressed all four CodeRabbit review findings on PR #15: packages/include/README.md OTOI build example corrected -std=c++20 -> -std=c++23; packages/otoi/src/OTOIManager.cpp source.uri and source.inline_doc now emitted independently instead of as an else-if chain so mutually-exclusive sources are still flagged; detectConflicts now uses the existing tier_from_string helper and skips unknown tier keys (std::nullopt) instead of silently defaulting to Tier::Project; packages/sleepwalker/tests/standalone_test.cpp gained a local process-id helper with a conditional <unistd.h> include (POSIX) and std::rand fallback (non-POSIX), replacing all ::getpid() call sites so the runner compiles without relying on transitive headers

Fixed packages/sleepwalker/src include paths — all four .cpp files now include <sleepwalker/X.h> (namespaced) instead of bare "X.h", matching the convention already used by toi and otoi and required for consumers that add packages/sleepwalker/include to their include path
Fixed packages/toi/src and packages/otoi/src bare local includes (TermsOfInteraction.h, TOITypes.h, OTOIManager.h, OTOITypes.h → namespaced forms) for the same consumer-facing reason

Fixed OTOI package latent C++23 issues: added missing #include <expected> to OTOIManager.h (header uses std::expected but never included it), corrected packages/otoi/CMakeLists.txt CXX_STANDARD 20→23 (std::expected is C++23; the CMake setting contradicted the source), added missing <set> include in OTOIManager.cpp

Fixed OTOIValidator::validate — it passed typed members (std::vector<OtoiAgent>, OtoiEnforcement, std::vector<OtoiSource>) to its own JSON-shaped section validators; now bridges the typed charter into the JSON shapes the validators expect. Fixed PolicyConflict.tier assignment (string tier key mapped to the Tier enum), and made resolveEnforcement public so OTOIManager::safeHonor can legally reuse it (pure resolver, no signature change)

Added packages/include/ vendored header directory for hermetic builds without vcpkg: nlohmann/json.hpp (official 3.11.3 single-header release, MIT), tl/expected.hpp (upstream v1.3.1, CC0 — required by packages/toi), and a minimal spdlog compatibility shim implementing the spdlog API subset used by the ports
Wrote packages/include/README.md documenting provenance, versions, licenses, per-package header requirements, and local build/verify commands

Added dependency-free standalone test runners (Catch2 unavailable locally) mirroring the Catch2 suites' core behaviors: packages/toi/tests/standalone_test.cpp, packages/otoi/tests/standalone_test.cpp, packages/sleepwalker/tests/standalone_test.cpp — written against the actual implemented APIs (TOI $-prefixed TOIDocument fields and safeParseTOI error codes; OTOI $otoi/$id charter fields and safeParseCharter/safeHonor)
Verified all three packages compile and pass their standalone suites end-to-end on this branch: TOI g++ -std=c++20, OTOI g++ -std=c++23, sleepwalker g++ -std=c++20 (g++ 15.2.0)
Re-verified after review fixes: TOI 25/25 (C++20), OTOI 8/8 (C++23), sleepwalker 84/84 (C++20); g++ 15.2.0; governance validation 22/22
blockers: No system-wide vcpkg/CMake toolchain on this machine — CMake-based builds and the Catch2 suites cannot be exercised here (pre-existing project-level limitation, documented in README packages/include/README.md)
decisions_made: Vendored official upstream single-headers (nlohmann/json 3.11.3, tl/expected 1.3.1) rather than trimming package dependencies — keeps packages/* source unchanged and matches upstream APIs exactly
spdlog is provided as a clearly-labeled local shim (not upstream code) because the ports only use a tiny API subset; README.md marks it for replacement by real spdlog under a full toolchain

Fixed all three packages' local includes via source edits (namespaced form) instead of adding root-level forwarding headers — matches the pattern reviewers already accepted for toi/otoi in PRs #10/#11

OTOIValidator::validate fix bridges typed members to the JSON shapes its existing section validators accept, instead of rewriting the validators — preserves all validation messages and the declared API

OTOI CMake corrected to C++23 rather than downgrading source to C++20 — the code legitimately targets C++23 (std::expected) and DECISIONS.md's dual error handling maps to std::expected there; TOI uses tl::expected at C++20 per its existing design
Standalone runners use plain assertions with pass/fail counters and a non-zero exit code on failure so they can serve as CI-able smoke tests without Catch2
decisions_pending: Whether CI should adopt the standalone runners as a required check (they build in ~2 min with no external deps) or keep governance-only validation

Top-level CMakeLists.txt aggregating all packages (per PLAN.md Section 10) — observed an in-progress Phase 6 effort on the desktop (untracked CMakeLists.txt + packages/asfdk/); not included in this PR
